title: Adaptive consumer-handoff pattern: TypeScript SDK async-iterable ↔ Web Streams bridge
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: SDK consumers use two primary consumption models in apps: async iteration (for Node/TS backend code) and Web Streams (for browser pipe/transform patterns). Currently our TypeScript SDK exposes separate helpers but developers face ergonomics and correctness problems when switching between the two: backpressure mismatches, cancellation semantics that leak, poor retry semantics across intermittent network disconnects, and no clear pattern for handoff between multiple concurrent consumers.

Goal: Implement an 'adaptive consumer-handoff' primitive in the TypeScript SDK that exposes a single source (the SDK stream) with first-class interoperability between AsyncIterator and ReadableStream consumers. The primitive should: preserve backpressure signals, support graceful cancellation and resume with retry tokens, enable dual-consumer handoff (one consumer can transfer ownership to another without data loss), and be lightweight for high-throughput scenarios.

Non-goals: This task does not add server-side resume support; we will implement client-only resume tokens that replay cached prefixes when available. We also will not change existing network protocols — only SDK runtime behavior.
acceptance_criteria: API: provide a single StreamProxy object with methods: [Symbol.asyncIterator](), toWebStream(): ReadableStream, and transferTo(newConsumer: 'async' | 'web') -> Promise<void>

Backpressure preserved: when a Web Stream consumer applies backpressure (by pausing reads), the underlying socket/transport batching is reduced within one RTT where possible (measured in integration tests)

Cancellation consistent: calling .cancel() on ReadableStream or calling return() on async iterator triggers the same AbortSignal and closes underlying transport; no unobserved memory growth in long-running tests

Retry/resume: transient network disconnects recover using a client-side resume token; SDK retries should resume from last acknowledged message when server supports incremental fetch, fallback to replay cached prefix when not supported
Dual-consumer handoff: tests demonstrate safe transfer from async iterator consumer to Web Stream consumer and vice versa with no message duplication or loss
Cross-platform: unit/integration tests pass on Node 18+, Deno (latest), and Chromium-based browsers via Playwright
Telemetry: emit instrumentation events for handoff, cancellation, retry, and backpressure (low-cardinality) and wire into existing SDK metrics
Docs: add a short guide and three examples (async-only, web-only, handoff pattern) in the SDK docs site
technical_notes: Design: StreamProxy will internally own a bounded ring buffer + rAF-like microtask pump that bridges between async iterator pulls and ReadableStream pulls. It exposes a single AbortController that is shared by both surfaces.

Backpressure: measure consumer queueLength and adaptively lower prefetch size. For Web Streams, use a TransformStream that forwards chunks and calls controller.desiredSize to detect backpressure. For async iterator, treat each next() as an explicit pull and keep small prefetch policy (default 2).

Cancellation: both .cancel() (ReadableStreamDefaultReader) and iterator.return() will call StreamProxy.close('client_cancel'), which sets error state and calls transport.abort(). Ensure AbortSignal.reason is set for telemetry.

Retry: when network disconnect occurs, SDK will call configured retry policy. On retry, StreamProxy will attempt to request server resume using last server-ack offset if the model/endpoint supports it. If not supported, the client will reconstruct state by replaying cached prefix (bounded to 64KB by default) and then append resumed stream. Resume token format: base64-encoded JSON {endpoint, model, offset, checksum}.

Dual-consumer handoff: transferTo(newConsumer) will drain current in-flight chunk to the new consumer only after its pull handshake succeeds. For atomicity, ack semantics are internal to StreamProxy; the primitive will provide per-chunk idempotency keys so downstream can dedupe if needed.

Edge cases: when both consumers read concurrently, StreamProxy queues one active consumer and returns a helpful runtime error if concurrent consumption is attempted without transferTo(). This avoids subtle interleaving bugs.

Compatibility: implement helpers: readableFromAsyncIterator(it, options) and asyncIteratorFromReadable(stream, options) inside SDK; these should prefer native built-ins where available and fall back to polyfills documented in migration guide.
Performance targets: additional median latency overhead <= 0.7ms for triaged microbenchmarks; memory overhead <= 1.5x baseline for sustained 1k msg/s workload on Node with default buffer size

Testing: add unit-tests for cancellation, handoff, backpressure; add stress tests running against a local fake transport that emits token bursts and random disconnects; add Playwright-based browser tests for pipeTo/pipeThrough scenarios
implementation_plan: Spike (2d): build a prototype StreamProxy that bridges an AsyncGenerator to a ReadableStream using a TransformStream and measure overhead
API Review (1d): propose public method names and idioms to SDK API review; gather feedback from DX and platform teams
Core Implementation (3d): implement ring buffer, pump, backpressure heuristics, and transferTo API in ts-sdk-runtime package
Retry integration (2d): integrate with existing retry policy module; implement resume token encoding/decoding and server-compat fallback
Tests (3d): unit, integration, and Playwright coverage; create stress harness and track memory/latency
Docs & Examples (1d): add docs page with migration tips and three code examples
PRs and Reviews (1d): address feedback, merge, and cut release branch for ts-sdk-2.4.0
comments: 2025-02-14 Aisha Kapoor: Ticket created after spike discussion with DX. Initial scope drafted.

2025-02-16 Diego Martinez: Completed 2-day spike. Prototype shows TransformStream bridge works and overhead is ~0.6ms per message for small payloads. Uploaded prototype: https://gist.github.com/redwood/streamproxy-proto
2025-02-18 Linnea Park (DX): Reviewed API. Suggested renaming transferTo -> handoff for clarity; decided to keep transferTo for discoverability but add handoff alias in docs.
2025-02-20 Samir Patel (PM): Prioritized to P1 for next SDK release. Agreed to default to conservative prefetch=2 and expose config for power users.
2025-02-24 Diego Martinez: Implemented first pass of queue and backpressure heuristics. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/1293 — requesting review from runtime team.
2025-02-27 QA: Found edge case where iterator.return() didn't wait for in-flight transfer; added gating promise to ensure atomic handoff. Test case added.
qa_notes: Stress test setup: run fake-transport at 1k msg/s for 10m with 5% random disconnects. Verify no memory growth >20MB beyond baseline and no message duplication.
Browser tests: Playwright script to verify pipeThrough transform then transferTo async iterator and vice versa. Test Chrome and Firefox.
Metrics to collect: handoff_count, cancel_count, retry_count, avg_queue_len, median_handoff_latency
